title.narrative: Strengthening African Civil Society and Governments’ leadership and voices on Climate Change

description.narrative: The decisions agreed at COP 26 made progress towards addressing the climate crisis but fell short of key expectations and asks of the vulnerable countries, including the Africa Group. The COP failed to raise the twice promised $100bn annual climate funding to vulnerable countries, did not close the mitigation and adaptation ambition gaps in line with staying below 1.5°C and didn’t establish the much needed financing facility for loss and damage. The science and message from leaders from vulnerable developing nations and organisations is unequivocal; failure to effectively implement the Paris Agreement and close the mitigation, adaptation, and financial gaps in this decade will mean that the opportunity to make the world safe for the present and future generations will be lost. 2022 is yet another critical year and an opportunity for ensuring meaningful global action on climate change. COP27 to be held in November 2022 in Egypt, on African soil, provides an opportunity for the continent to ensure that fair and ambitious outcome that meet the needs of the climate vulnerable countries and communities is met. As the COP hosts and with the right leadership, Africa can play a crucial role in shaping the outcome and creating space for the correct priorities. Africa remains the most vulnerable continent severely affected by climate change. International climate policy and processes including mobilisation around COP 27 presents opportunities to catalyse green and resilient investments in the continent. Despite the challenges and opportunities presented by climate change, Africa is the least engaged region on climate diplomacy and there is currently minimal public debate on clean energy and climate change. This is because there are structural barriers, including capacity gaps both within national and regional African decision-making bodies, as well as within civil society and other non-state actors that could otherwise support enhanced climate leadership. This must change in the runup to the African COP in 2022 and beyond. Power Shift Africa will help facilitate informed and effective participation of Africa in the global climate change negotiations including at the UNFCCC through building capacities of government officials and CSOs, support effective media campaign and promoting ambitious and equitable positions and demands, and helping to secure a fair, robust and science-based outcomes at COP 27 and COP 28.
